### Why EPFO Employment History Is the Most Reliable Work History Check in India


When a candidate hands you a resume listing three previous employers, you have no way to know if those companies actually employed them. Experience letters can be fabricated. Reference phone numbers can be fake. LinkedIn profiles can be inflated.


But EPFO (Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation) records cannot be fabricated by candidates. Here is why.


Every employer with 20 or more employees is legally required to register with EPFO and contribute to each employee’s Provident Fund account. These contributions are linked to the employee’s UAN (Universal Account Number), which is in turn linked to their Aadhaar and PAN. When an employer makes a PF contribution for an employee, the EPFO database records the company name, the employee’s joining date, the exit date, and the monthly contribution amount. **The candidate has no ability to add, edit, or delete entries in this database. Only the employer can create entries by making PF contributions.**


This makes EPFO employment history the single most tamper-proof source of work history data available to Indian HR teams.


The data confirms why this matters. EY’s study of over one million background screenings found that **85% of all discrepancies were caught through employment verification** , not identity checks, not education checks, but employment history. AuthBridge’s Workforce Fraud Files H1 FY26 reported that **4.33% of white-collar candidates carry at least one discrepancy** . And the most common type of employment fraud is not a small exaggeration, it is **entirely fabricated employers** (EY found 32% of flagged candidates had listed companies they never worked for).


This guide reviews **5 platforms that let HR teams check EPFO employment history** before a new hire’s first day, from instant self-serve tools to API-based solutions and enterprise verification services.


**What this guide covers:**


- What EPFO employment history data contains and how to read it
- 5 platforms compared on speed, cost, and data completeness
- Step-by-step process for checking a new hire’s EPFO history
- EPFO data vs. manual reference checks, head-to-head comparison
- 5 specific red flags EPFO data reveals that resumes hide


### What EPFO Employment History Actually Shows


When you check a candidate’s EPFO employment history using their UAN, the database returns a record for every employer that contributed to their Provident Fund. Here is exactly what each entry contains and what it means for HR.


#### Data Fields in an EPFO Employment History Record


Field What It Shows What HR Should Check


**Employer/Establishment Name** The company name as registered with EPFO Does this match the company listed on the resume?


**Date of Joining** The date the employee was added to PF by this employer Does this match the joining date claimed on the resume?


**Date of Exit** The date PF contributions stopped (exit or termination) Does this match the exit date on the resume? Any unexplained gaps?


**Member ID** The employee’s PF account number with this employer Confirms the employee actually had a PF account at this company


**Monthly Wage** The wage on which PF was calculated Roughly validates the salary band claimed by the candidate


**PF Contribution Amount** The employer’s and employee’s PF contribution Confirms active employment (contributions mean actual payroll)


**UAN** Universal Account Number linking all employers Single number ties together the candidate’s full employment chain


#### How to Read EPFO Employment History as an HR Team


What You See What It Means Hiring Decision


All resume employers appear in EPFO with matching dates Candidate’s work history is genuine Proceed with onboarding


Resume lists Company X, but EPFO has no record of Company X Candidate never worked there (or Company X did not contribute PF) Ask candidate to explain; likely fabricated if Company X has 20+ employees


EPFO shows Company Y, but resume does not mention Company Y Candidate hid a previous employer (possible termination or short stint) Investigate why this employer was omitted


Joining/exit dates differ by more than 1–2 months Candidate inflated tenure Ask candidate to clarify the discrepancy


EPFO shows overlapping employment at two companies Candidate was employed at two places simultaneously (moonlighting) Assess per your company’s dual employment policy


No EPFO records at all despite claimed 5+ years of experience Candidate worked only in informal/unregistered sector, or UAN is wrong Request alternative proof; not necessarily fraud


#### Why EPFO Data Is More Reliable Than Other Employment Verification Methods


Method Data Source Can Candidate Manipulate? Speed Completeness


**EPFO/UAN check** Government PF database No — only employers can create records Minutes Every EPFO-registered employer


Experience letter Candidate-provided document Yes — letters can be fabricated or edited Instant (but unreliable) Only what candidate chooses to share


Reference call to previous employer Phone call to HR Partially — fake numbers, colluding contacts 1–5 days (if HR responds) Only if previous HR cooperates


LinkedIn profile check Candidate-managed profile Yes — candidates control their own profile Instant (but unreliable) Only what candidate chooses to display


Manual BGV (employer outreach) Third-party verifier contacts employer Low — but depends on employer response 2–7 days Only for employers who respond

### 2. EPFO Member Portal — Free Government Portal (Candidate Self-Service)


**What it does:** The EPFO Unified Member Portal allows employees (not employers) to log in with their UAN and view their own service history, including every employer that contributed PF, joining dates, exit dates, and contribution details. In 2026, EPFO also launched a Service History feature that helps members trace old PF accounts across employers.


**EPFO employment history details:**


Feature Details


Data source EPFO (direct government portal)


Input required Employee’s UAN + Aadhaar-linked mobile OTP


Data returned Service history: employer names, joining/exit dates, member IDs, contributions


Speed Minutes (after OTP authentication)


Cost Free


Output On-screen service history (can be screenshot or PDF-printed)


Who can access The employee only (requires their UAN + OTP)


**How HR teams use it:** Ask the candidate to log into the EPFO portal, download their service history, and share it with HR. This is free but relies entirely on the candidate’s cooperation and honesty. The candidate controls what they share and could potentially share a modified screenshot.


**Strengths:**


- Completely free — no cost to the company
- Most comprehensive EPFO data (full service history, contributions, passbook)
- Direct government source — the most authoritative employment data
- New Service History feature traces old and transferred PF accounts


**Limitations:**


- HR cannot access it directly — only the employee can log in with their UAN and OTP
- Candidate controls what they share (can omit screenshots, edit printouts)
- No independent verification — you are trusting the candidate’s submitted output
- No PDF report generated for the employer’s files
- No additional identity checks (PAN, Voter ID, DL)
- Not scalable — each candidate must individually log in and share
- Candidates may not know their UAN or have access to their registered mobile number


**Best for:** A free starting point where you ask candidates to share their EPFO service history voluntarily. However, this is not independent verification — the candidate controls the data. For tamper-proof employer-driven EPFO checks, use SalaryBox Verify.

### 5 Red Flags EPFO Data Reveals That Resumes Hide


#### Red Flag 1: The Ghost Employer


**What the resume says:** “Worked at Pinnacle Solutions Pvt Ltd, 2019–2022, Senior Analyst”


**What EPFO shows:** No record of Pinnacle Solutions Pvt Ltd contributing PF for this candidate. Ever.


**What it means:** If Pinnacle Solutions has 20+ employees and is EPFO-registered, the candidate never worked there. If the company exists but is not EPFO-registered (under 20 employees), ask for alternative proof. If the company does not exist at all, this is outright fabrication.


**How often this happens:** EY found that 32% of flagged candidates had listed employers they never worked for.


#### Red Flag 2: The Inflated Tenure


**What the resume says:** “ABC Technologies, January 2020 – December 2023 (4 years)”


**What EPFO shows:** ABC Technologies, PF contributions from March 2021 to June 2022 (15 months).


**What it means:** The candidate inflated a 15-month stint into a 4-year tenure. They either joined later than claimed, left earlier than claimed, or both.


#### Red Flag 3: The Hidden Employer


**What the resume says:** “ABC Corp (2018–2020) → XYZ Ltd (2020–2023)”


**What EPFO shows:** ABC Corp (2018–2020) → **DEF Services (2020–2021)** → XYZ Ltd (2021–2023)


**What it means:** The candidate worked at DEF Services for about a year and chose not to mention it. Possible reasons: short stint, termination, performance issues, or the company’s reputation. Always ask why an employer was omitted.


#### Red Flag 4: The Moonlighter


**What the resume says:** “Currently employed at ABC Corp since 2022”


**What EPFO shows:** PF contributions from both ABC Corp AND GHI Pvt Ltd during the same months in 2023–2024.


**What it means:** The candidate was receiving salary (and PF) from two employers simultaneously. This is dual employment. AuthBridge H2 2025 data showed a 4.99% moonlighting rate in their screening data.


#### Red Flag 5: The Fake Gap


**What the resume says:** “Took a career break for higher studies, 2021–2022”


**What EPFO shows:** PF contributions from JKL Industries throughout 2021–2022.


**What it means:** The candidate was not on a career break. They were employed at JKL Industries and chose to hide it. The “higher studies” explanation was fabricated to cover an employer they do not want you to know about.


> **Every one of these red flags is invisible on a resume, undetectable in an interview, and unverifiable through a reference call. Only EPFO data catches them — because only government records are outside the candidate’s control.**


#### FAQs: EPFO Employment History Verification for New Hires


###### 1. What is EPFO employment history verification?


EPFO employment history verification checks a candidate’s work history against the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation government database. Using the candidate’s UAN (Universal Account Number), the verification returns every employer that contributed PF for them, along with joining dates, exit dates, and contribution details. This data is government-maintained and cannot be fabricated by the candidate.


###### 2. How is EPFO verification different from calling the previous employer?


EPFO verification queries a government database where records are created by employers through PF contributions. The candidate cannot add or edit entries. Manual reference calls rely on reaching the previous employer’s HR, who may not respond, may share limited information, or whose number may be fake. EPFO data is tamper-proof; reference calls are not.


###### 3. What does EPFO employment history cost to check?


SalaryBox Verify charges Rs. 499 per candidate for EPFO employment history along with PAN, Voter ID, and DL verification. Attestr and SurePass offer API access at custom per-call pricing (requires developer integration). AuthBridge includes EPFO data as part of enterprise packages at Rs. 1,500–Rs. 5,000+ per candidate. The EPFO Member Portal is free but only the candidate (not the employer) can access it.


###### 4. Can EPFO verification detect moonlighting?


Yes. If a candidate has PF contributions from two employers during the same time period, EPFO data will show overlapping employment. This indicates the candidate was dual-employed (moonlighting). AuthBridge H2 2025 data showed a 4.99% moonlighting rate in their screening results.


###### 5. What if the candidate does not know their UAN?


Candidates can retrieve their UAN from the EPFO Member Portal using their Aadhaar number, PAN, or bank account details. They can also find it on their PF passbook or salary slips from previous employers. Include UAN as a required field in your offer acceptance or onboarding form so candidates provide it before Day 1.


###### 6. Does EPFO verification work for candidates who worked at startups?


It depends on whether the startup was EPFO-registered. Companies with 20 or more employees must register with EPFO. Many startups below this threshold or in their early stages do not contribute PF, so their employees will not have EPFO records from those roles. For candidates with startup experience, EPFO will show only the employers that contributed PF.


###### 7. Can EPFO verification detect fake employers listed on a resume?


Yes, this is its primary strength. If a candidate claims they worked at “Pinnacle Solutions Pvt Ltd” for 3 years but EPFO has no record of Pinnacle Solutions contributing PF for them, the claim is likely fabricated. EY found that 32% of flagged candidates had listed employers they never worked for.


###### 8. How long does EPFO employment history verification take?


On SalaryBox Verify, EPFO data returns within minutes. API-based tools (Attestr, SurePass) return data in seconds. AuthBridge’s manual employment verification takes 2–5 business days because they combine database checks with phone calls to previous employers.


###### 9. Should I check EPFO employment history for every new hire?


Yes. At Rs. 499 on SalaryBox Verify (which includes identity checks too), there is no cost justification for skipping it. EY found that 85% of all discrepancies are caught through employment verification. Skipping EPFO checks for junior or mid-level hires — where AuthBridge data shows most discrepancies occur — leaves your biggest hiring risk unaddressed.


###### 10. What should I do if EPFO data contradicts the resume?


First, share the specific discrepancy with the candidate and ask for an explanation. Minor date differences (1–2 months) may be due to probation periods or PF registration delays. A completely missing employer on EPFO is more serious. Hidden employers (present in EPFO, absent from resume) require investigation. Document the candidate’s response and your decision in the verification file for audit purposes.
